# Numerical golden fixtures

`MunkP_one_ray.env` is derived from Acoustics Toolbox `v2023.5`
`tests/Munk/MunkB_ray.env` at commit
`475108519289c6fb488b58980c644ea14eccc604`. Modifications are limited to the
title, one source depth, one launch angle, and a 10.1 km trace box.

The other `.env` files are small, project-authored, reduced, or unmodified
official cases. They cover every `N/C/P/S/Q/A` SSP algorithm, Cartesian
geometric-hat eigenrays and arrivals, Cartesian geometric-Gaussian arrivals,
and all three pressure-field coherence modes, including geometric, simple-
Gaussian, and Cerveny beams. The `.ray`, `.arr`, and pressure CSV values were generated from the unmodified
`v2023.5` Fortran source using GNU Fortran 14.2.0 on Apple arm64 with:

```text
-O1 -ffast-math -funroll-all-loops -fomit-frame-pointer -std=gnu
```

The pressure CSV files were extracted from the generated `.shd` records in
range-major, then depth-major order. `InternalReflection.irc` and its `.brc`
check values were generated by BOUNCE v2023.5 from a seven-sample reduction of
`tests/TabRefCoef/neggradB.env`. The elastic and grain reflection CSVs were
generated by small Fortran harnesses containing the corresponding unmodified
`bellhop.f90::Reflect2D` branches. `DickinsCritical` and `ParaBotCritical`
were generated by the pinned Linux x86-64 container under `tools/reference`;
they exercise compiler-sensitive minimum-step branches and are checked by
`tools/reference/check-critical-rays.sh`. The legacy binary containers are not
committed.

`ShadedField`, `FreeFGB_grid`, `Field_CervenyF`, and `Field_CervenyW` were
generated by the same pinned Linux x86-64 container; they add numerical
coverage for the source beam pattern, Francois-Garrison volume attenuation,
and the space-filling/WKB Cerveny width options.

`Field_ThorpLine` and `Field_BioLine` derive from `Field_G`: 33 samples each,
coherent hat / incoherent Gaussian line-source scaling, Thorp at 5 kHz and
biological loss at 1 kHz (two overlapping layers, knots on their edges).
`SimpleGaussian_eigen` changes `GeoHat_eigen` to `ES`: all three trajectories /
314 coordinates are compared, replacing count-only evidence. `BeamShift`
changes `ElasticReflection` to `RG    S`; a bottom bounce activates the shift,
and disabling it changes the coordinates beyond the unchanged ray tolerance.
All four use the fixed Linux oracle above; three fresh runs have identical
SHD/RAY bytes. CSV extraction reads little-endian complex32 pressures from
SHD records 10+depth (zero-based), ordered range then depth, without rounding.
Full acceptance reruns these inputs against fresh Fortran (not Rust goldens).

The seven `Field_WkbGradientC/R`, `Field_LineS`, `Field_LineCervenyC/R`
and `Field_LineSemiG/B` cases are the constructed two-source shelf inputs from
`tools/reference/bellhop-business.py`. Each CSV contains all 30 complex pressures,
in source-major, range-major, depth-major order. They are extracted without
rounding from unmodified pinned Linux Fortran SHD, not Rust output. These lock
WKB signed-zero square-root branches and the reference's default-real BETA,
line-scaling pi and semi-coherent SQRT(2) constants. The raw WKB SHD files are
byte-identical across three runs. `Field_NearGaussian` adds a 2–10 m line-source
shelf regression for the Gaussian diffraction floor's default-real `0.2`.
See the business coverage report for provenance.

This small golden catches computation-order regressions. The eventual pinned
Linux differential container remains the authoritative cross-platform oracle.
